bands.1:
The Soggy Biscuit sails into Quillstone Reef. Tall stone spikes poke out of the water like giant pens.

A leafy Kelpwick glides past. A turtle called a Tocktle ticks like a clock. A tiny Biffoon punches a shell to bits.

"Twelve Creatures already!" says Tully.

Then Zed points down. Under the water, something glows gold. It is a big glass dome. A sign on it says, "MAXX'S REEF RESCUE CENTRE. NO PEEKING."

"That's his base," you say.

"The air vents are on the north side," says Wren quietly.

Suddenly, an old ship covered in barnacles blocks your way. A huge man stands on the deck. He has a long white beard. A little blue crab sits on his shoulder. It snips its claws. Snip, snip.

"Ho, ho, ho!" says Mo. "Is it Christmas?"

"I am not THAT Claus," the man booms. "I am Captain Clause. Mine has an E on the end and a much worse temper."

"Nice boat," says Zed.

"That is not a sentence," says Captain Clause. "That is a crumb. Who did what?"

"Your boat looks nice," says Zed.

"Better."

The crab is called Clawsette. She snips the air again.

Captain Clause tells you about the dome. Maxx's divers come at night with gold nets. Half the reef's Creatures are gone. Clause tried to stop them. Maxx filmed him yelling. The video was called "Grumpy Old Sea Man." Now nobody believes him.

"Will you help us?" you ask.

"Build me strong sentences, Captain," he says. "Win my badge. Then I will help."

Just then, Gus fishes a soggy gold card out of the water.

"Round-up night is Friday. Target: the crab. From M."

Clawsette stops snipping. She hides in Captain Clause's beard.

"Then we have until Friday," says Captain Clause.

bands.4:
The Soggy Biscuit chugs into Quillstone Reef just after sunrise, coughing smoke from its tired old engine. Tall stone spires poke out of the sea like enormous pen nibs, and the water around them is so clear that you can count every fish darting between the coral.

The reef is buzzing with life. A leafy Kelpwick drifts past, its fronds rippling like ribbons in a breeze. A Tocktle paddles by with a clock face on its shell, ticking softly as its hands sweep round. A tiny Biffoon, no bigger than your thumb, punches a shell so hard that it explodes into glittering fragments.

"Twelve Creatures in two minutes," says Tully, scribbling furiously in her notebook. "That's a reef record and a personal best. The Reef Rays haven't scored that fast all season."

In the galley, Mo is stirring a pot of seaweed spag bol that is slowly turning purple. "It's a bit crunchy," he admits, "but in a fishy way."

Then Zed points over the side. Deep under the water, something glows gold. It's an enormous glass dome squatting on the reef floor like a golden jellyfish, ringed with spotlights. A sign bolted to its side says, "MAXX'S REEF RESCUE CENTRE. NO PEEKING. THIS MEANS YOU."

"That's his base," you say.

"The air vents are on the north side," Wren murmurs, almost to herself.

Before anyone can say a word, an old ship crusted with barnacles swings across your path, its patched sails cracking in the wind. On the deck stands a huge man with a snowy beard that reaches all the way to his belt. A small blue crab perches on his shoulder, snipping its claws with a sound like tiny scissors.

"Ho, ho, ho!" calls Mo. "Is it Christmas already?"

"I am not THAT Claus," the man booms, in a voice that rattles the portholes. "I am Captain Clause. Mine has an E on the end and a considerably worse temper."

"Nice boat," says Zed.

"That is not a sentence," says Captain Clause. "That is a crumb. Who did what? Tell me properly, or don't tell me at all."

Zed thinks so hard that his forehead wrinkles. "Your boat looks very nice."

"Better," says the captain. "Short sentences are fine. Broken ones are not."

Mo holds up his pot. "Spag bol, Captain Clause? It's a sentence on its own: Mo cooked lunch."

"And what happened next?" asks the captain, sniffing it.

"Everyone was sick," admits Mo.

"Now THAT," says Captain Clause, "is a story."

The crab is called Clawsette, and she snips the air as if she agrees with every word.

Captain Clause invites you aboard and tells you about the dome. Every night, Maxx's divers swim out with gold nets and slip away with the rarest Creatures they can find. Half the reef's Creatures have already vanished. When Clause rowed out to stop the divers, Maxx filmed him shouting and waving his arms. The video was called "Grumpy Old Sea Man Yells at Reef," and it got twelve million views in a single day. Now nobody in the archipelago believes a word he says.

"Will you help us get them back?" you ask.

Captain Clause studies you for a long, uncomfortable time, his bushy eyebrows lowered. "Build me sentences that hold water, Captain," he says at last. "Win my badge. Then, and only then, I will stand with you."

Just then, Gus fishes a soggy gold card out of a drifting net. It smells powerfully of old prawns, which Gus clearly considers a bonus. He reads it aloud.

"Round-up night is Friday. Target: the crab. From M."

Clawsette stops snipping. She burrows deep into Captain Clause's beard until only one trembling eye pokes out.

Captain Clause's face goes hard as the stone spires. "Then we have until Friday," he says.
